cards.back: A hard natural material found in the ground.
cards.say: rock. A hard natural material found in the ground.

cards.back: For example granite, sandstone and limestone. Slate and marble are rocks too.
cards.say: Name three kinds of rock.. For example granite, sandstone and limestone. Slate and marble are rocks too.

cards.back: A permeable material lets water soak into it. Sandy soil is permeable.
cards.say: permeable. A permeable material lets water soak into it. Sandy soil is permeable.

cards.back: An impermeable material does not let water soak in. Slate is impermeable.
cards.say: impermeable. An impermeable material does not let water soak in. Slate is impermeable.

cards.back: A rock that is difficult to scratch, such as granite.
cards.say: hard rock. A rock that is difficult to scratch, such as granite.

cards.back: A rock that is easy to scratch or crumble, such as chalk.
cards.say: soft rock. A rock that is easy to scratch or crumble, such as chalk.

cards.front: How can you test how hard a rock is?
cards.back: Try to scratch it with a coin or a nail.
cards.say: How can you test how hard a rock is? Try to scratch it with a coin or a nail.

cards.front: Why is slate used for roofs?
cards.back: It is hard and impermeable so rain runs off.
cards.say: Why is slate used for roofs? It is hard and impermeable so rain runs off.

cards.front: Why is marble used for statues?
cards.back: It is smooth and can be carved. It also looks beautiful.
cards.say: Why is marble used for statues? It is smooth and can be carved. It also looks beautiful.

cards.back: A mixture of tiny bits of rock and bits of dead plants and animals.
cards.say: soil. A mixture of tiny bits of rock and bits of dead plants and animals.

cards.back: Dead leaves and plants that have rotted in soil. It makes soil rich.
cards.say: What is humus? Dead leaves and plants that have rotted in soil. It makes soil rich.

cards.front: What are sand and clay in soil?
cards.back: Tiny particles of rock.
cards.say: What are sand and clay in soil? Tiny particles of rock.

cards.front: Which soil lets water drain fast, sandy soil or clay soil?
cards.back: Sandy soil.
cards.say: Which soil lets water drain fast, sandy soil or clay soil? Sandy soil.

cards.back: Clay soil.
cards.say: Which soil holds water best? Clay soil.

cards.front: Why is soil important to plants?
cards.back: Plants root in it and get water and nutrients from it.
cards.say: Why is soil important to plants? Plants root in it and get water and nutrients from it.

cards.back: The remains or marks of a living thing that died long ago, kept in rock.
cards.say: fossil. The remains or marks of a living thing that died long ago, kept in rock.

cards.back: A dead animal or plant is buried in mud or sand. Over millions of years the mud hardens into rock and the shape stays.
cards.say: How does a fossil form? A dead animal or plant is buried in mud or sand. Over millions of years the mud hardens into rock and the shape stays.

cards.front: Where do we often find fossils?
cards.back: In rocks such as limestone and sandstone.
cards.say: Where do we often find fossils? In rocks such as limestone and sandstone.

cards.back: What plants and animals lived long ago.
cards.say: What can fossils tell us? What plants and animals lived long ago.

cards.front: Which animal parts are most likely to become fossils?
cards.back: Hard parts such as bones, teeth and shells.
cards.say: Which animal parts are most likely to become fossils? Hard parts such as bones, teeth and shells.

cards.front: True or false: Soil is made only of rock.
cards.back: False. Soil also has dead plants and animals, air and water.
cards.say: True or false: Soil is made only of rock. False. Soil also has dead plants and animals, air and water.
